subdomain.name: Telemetry Ingestion & Processing
subdomain.capability: Continuous, high-throughput ingestion of raw 1Hz time-series sensor payloads (heart rate, power, cadence, ground contact time, respiration, swim stroke telemetry) from IoT edge devices, bike computers and smart wearables; enforces Sensor Metric Boundary, reconciles out-of-order backfills and buffers windowed telemetry streams for streaming analytics (PulseStream Engine).
subdomain.why_distinct: Core domain of the endurance athletic analytics platform: owns the rules for validating, reordering and immutably recording raw telemetry before any downstream analytics.

ubiquitous_language.definition: Individual 1Hz data point from a sensor.
Raw payload received at the ingestion entry point, carrying Telemetry Samples.
Device-generated epoch timestamp; the chronological ordering key.
Arrival time at ingestion; never used for ordering.
60-second window within which delayed out-of-order packets are re-indexed by t_device.
Physical physiological/mechanical limits a sample metric must satisfy.
Status flag tagged on invalid samples; payload is retained.
Demand-driven flow control so burst loads and slow downstream consumers never cause blocking I/O.

bounded_contexts.name: Telemetry Ingestion
bounded_contexts.responsibility: Accept Ingress Packets, validate Telemetry Samples against Sensor Metric Boundary, reorder late packets within the Backfill Reorder Window by t_device, and append samples/revisions to immutable storage.
in_scope: Sensor Metric Boundary validation and VALIDATION_FAILED tagging
Append-only raw record and revision storage
invariants: Every raw 1Hz Telemetry Sample is validated before downstream propagation: HR 30-240 BPM, Power 0-2500W, Cadence 0-220 RPM, Swimming Pace >45 sec/100m.
Invalid samples are tagged VALIDATION_FAILED and the underlying payload is never dropped.
Out-of-order packets delayed up to 60 seconds are re-indexed chronologically by t_device, not t_ingress.
Raw time-series records are strictly append-only; corrections and backfilled frames append new event revisions for auditability.
Ingestion entry point keeps backpressure control with zero blocking I/O on thread pools.
source_of_truth: Append-only raw telemetry record and revision history

bounded_contexts.name: Telemetry Stream Distribution
bounded_contexts.responsibility: Buffer windowed telemetry streams and broadcast validated events to downstream event streams under Reactive Stream Backpressure.
invariants: Broadcasting honors Reactive Stream Backpressure; no blocking I/O on thread pools.
Only samples already validated/tagged by Telemetry Ingestion are propagated.
source_of_truth: Derived windowed buffers (non-authoritative; raw record stays in Telemetry Ingestion)

assumptions.item: Ambiguity: delivery posture of Ingress Packets (at-most-once vs at-least-once) and the identity distinguishing a retry from a new revision are unstated. If natural identity (device, metric, t_device) is used, is the mutable payload value part of it? Including it turns corrections into new events but makes retries of corrections indistinguishable; excluding it makes corrections look like duplicates.
assumptions.impact_on_boundaries: Dedup duty inside Telemetry Ingestion; determines whether corrections append revisions.

assumptions.item: Named metrics without stated ranges: ground contact time, respiration, swim stroke telemetry; swim pace only has lower bound >45 sec/100m, no upper bound. No ranges invented; treated as unbounded (no boundary check) pending operator answer.
assumptions.impact_on_boundaries: Sensor Metric Boundary validation scope in Telemetry Ingestion.

assumptions.item: Packets arriving later than the 60-second Backfill Reorder Window are unspecified (reject, append as revision, or flag); treated as open question.
assumptions.impact_on_boundaries: Reorder invariant ownership stays in Telemetry Ingestion.

assumptions.item: Stream buffering/broadcast split into a separate context because cadence and consumers differ from ingestion; description names it a single domain focus, so it could merge.
Description does not state that security is unnecessary; no security_directive recorded, so security is required. Authentication of devices is unspecified.
